answer: Stop sybils with a marble inlet raven: an agent stakes a bond for one marble inlet. Each cycle a raven flies the inlet and files its wing mark; verifiers match the mark to the marble gate, voiding an inlet whose mark is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 inlets at 18x: each mark fits one marble and one raven, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents fly once and keep rights.
